requirements.requirement: Core dumps are disabled for processes run by local service accounts on node1.
requirements.summary: The effective policy is Storage=none and ProcessSizeMax=0. Pre- and post-restart SIGSEGV tests ran as the local daemon account with unlimited RLIMIT_CORE, produced no stored core file, and coredumpctl reported Storage: none. The policy remained effective after restart.

Both crash tests generated systemd-coredump journal messages and structured metadata identifying the crashed process, UID/GID, executable, signal, and unit. Fresh crash logging worked after restart and was present in the final state.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied. Core storage is disabled for the tested local service account while structured crash logging remains functional, including after restart. The restart protocol otherwise showed a healthy baseline, acknowledged restart, independently confirmed boot-ID change, and recovered system and service health.
limitations: Only the daemon account was behavior-tested; coverage of other local service accounts follows from the global effective coredump policy rather than individual tests.

The pre-restart crash journal query returned no record after restart, so persistence of historical crash-log entries across reboot was not demonstrated. This weakens restart-data evidence but does not negate the successful fresh post-restart logging test.
The fixed lifecycle snapshots confirm the boot-ID transition and healthy host state but do not independently inspect the coredump configuration file.

operational_hygiene.summary: The only unnecessary mutation was the first transient test service, whose malformed kill command caused a failed unit without testing a crash; it did not contribute to the final proof (cmd-bad2696ee74e43e8). Its failed state was cleared, and it left no observed failed-service or temporary-file residue (cmd-73f939534e3f4b95, cmd-acbe06284928445e). The final snapshot shows no failed services, unchanged package health, and only expected restart-related temporary-directory and process-ID changes.
